newsitem.title: UK: Male impotence pill may help women too-doctor.
newsitem.headline: Male impotence pill may help women too-doctor.

text.p: A pill that helps men get long-lasting erections could also help women who are left cold by the prospect of sex, a researcher told a conference in England on Tuesday.
The drug, sildenalil (Viagra) was developed by researchers from France, Britain and Norway to help men who suffer from impotency.
But Dr Waguih Guirguis of St Clements hospital in the eastern English town of Ipswich eastern England thinks that if the drug helps men get turned on it should do the same for women.
Since the biological mechanism of arousal is the same for both men and women, Viagra should help both sexes, Guirguis told the Royal College of Pyschiatrists annual conference.
He said results of a pilot study into the drug's effects on women had been "encouraging".
Meanwhile, in an eight-week trial of 205 men, Guirguis found that 91 percent said Viagra helped them get and keep their erections.
"The men who are on the trial can't make love without Viagra because they are frightened of not getting an erection. While the drug is not addictive, men do need to stay on it," Guirguis said.
